title: Loose textures in Rust: a [[texture]] usage row, square power-of-two images, compressed families checked
note: A loose image your code samples gets a [[texture]] row (color, data or normal); make it square power-of-two; __render.assetIssues must not list it.
intent: Studio encodes each PNG or JPEG whose usage it knows into GPU-compressed KTX2 files beside it (bc on desktops, astc and etc2 on phones, all of them on the web, where a browser fetches only the one its GPU reads) and keeps the image as the fallback. A texture a model's material samples is known from its slot; a CC0 map is known from its role. A loose image your own code samples (a custom material's normal map, a mask, a flow map) is known only from a [[texture]] row in genex.toml with usage color, data or normal, never from its file name. Without one it ships as the image and state().__render.assetIssues names it texture-uncompressed. Make images square with a power-of-two side (an odd size is resized and its UVs stretch) and sample them with UVs from 0 to 1. After a build look at state().__render.textures: each texture's kind is the usage you meant and its family is bc, astc, etc2 or rgba8, not source. texture-family-refused means every size class it fits is full: use fewer or smaller textures of that kind. tangents-runtime names a normal-mapped model the import did not see: import it instead of loading it raw.
sketch:
# genex.toml
[[texture]]
path = "textures/water-normal.png"   # sampled by a custom material, so no model's slot says
usage = "normal"

[[texture]]
path = "textures/foam-mask.png"
usage = "data"                          # numbers, not colour: never sRGB-decoded
port: The facet that samples a loose texture owns its [[texture]] row; a texture a model's material samples is the model's and needs none.

evidence.note: [[texture]] rows, invalid-texture-usage, the KTX2 families per destination and the power-of-two resize.
__render.textures kind and family; __render.assetIssues texture-uncompressed, texture-family-refused, tangents-runtime.
